title: Flexi credit surge experiment and security questionnaire playbook
creator: Avery Collins
description: Run a multipart PLG experiment to test whether transient, usage-triggered credit top-ups ("flexi surges") increase activation and paid conversion for developer accounts, while simultaneously preparing a standardized security questionnaire playbook that shortens time-to-contract for interested enterprise trialists. This ticket coordinates experiment definition, analytics instrumentation, rollout gating, and the enterprise security/RFQ collateral to accelerate sales handoffs.
background: We have observed that a subset of free-tier/credit users hit early friction points during compute-intensive evals (long prompts, embeddings batches) and drop off before reaching a meaningful trial signal. Past experiments focused on static credit sizes and expiry windows. Sales and Solutions Engineering reported repeated delays from security question responses slowing enterprise pilots.
hypothesis: If we provide ephemeral, usage-triggered credit top-ups (surge events) during the first 14 days of signup and pair that with a pre-baked security questionnaire playbook for enterprise leads, then 7-day activation and 30-day paid conversion will increase without materially increasing cost per acquisition.
experiment_design: Arm A (control): existing free tier 1,000 tokens, 14-day expiry, no top-ups.

Arm B (flexi-surge): initial 500 tokens + up to 3 scheduled top-ups (500 tokens each) triggered when user attempts a request >=50% of balance within first 14 days. Top-ups expire 48 hours after grant.

Arm C (burst-window): 1,000 tokens + one large ephemeral burst (2,000 tokens) available if user hits a complexity threshold (embedding batch >50 vectors or generation >2,000 tokens) in the first 7 days.
Randomization: 1:1:1 seeded at account creation. Exclude internal/test accounts and enterprise SSO signups.
Duration: 12 weeks with an interim analysis at 4 weeks. Target N = 12k new signups total (4k per arm).
rollout_plan: Week 0: feature flag behind 'flexi-surge-experiment' with split allocation service and feature gating in sign-up flow.
Week 1: small canary (5% of allocation) to validate instrumentation and billing reconciliation.
Week 2-6: full 1:1:1 rollout to new signups across regions US/EU; monitor cost signals daily.
Stop criteria: spike in incremental cost per converting user > 3x baseline or error rate increase in billing reconciliation > 1%.
Rollout owners: PM (Riya Patel), Eng lead (Marco Nguyen), Analytics (Samira O'Neill), SE (Diego Ramos).
observability: Dashboards: experiment cohort KPIs, cost per cohort, top-up redemption heatmap (Datadog/Grafana).
Instrumentation: event names 'topup_granted', 'topup_redeemed', 'first_long_request', and token-burn reconciliation job updated (ENG-19122).
Alerts: daily delta >10% in activation or conversion triggers Slack channel #pm-experiments and PagerDuty to on-call for billing-team for reconciliation issues.
A/B analysis doc: link to Confluence with planned statistical tests and stopping rules.
security_playbook: Assemble canonical answers for the top 25 security questionnaire items requested by prospects (encryption, data residency, access controls, SOC/ISO attestations).
Create a templated one-page security summary (PDF) and a living Confluence 'security-playbook' that maps Qs to canonical artifacts (network diagrams, KMS architecture, retention policies).
Designate owners for rapid responses: Security (Priya Menon), Solutions Eng (Diego Ramos), Legal (Hannah Lee).

Automate distribution: when an account is flagged as 'enterprise-interest' in trial (conversion trigger or SE outreach), attach the security summary to the welcome email and open a pre-filled RFQ ticket for Security to complete.
risks: Cost: unexpected high redemption of top-ups by bots or heavy users could increase spend. Mitigation: rate-limit top-ups and add bot filtering in sign-up flow.
Gaming: users may create throwaway accounts to harvest top-ups. Mitigation: link redemption to email verification + device fingerprinting + ephemeral quota per IP range.
Enterprise trust: incomplete or outdated security artifacts could delay contracts. Mitigation: maintain a quarterly review cadence and auto-alert owners when attestation dates >90 days old.
Instrumentation drift: mis-tagged events may invalidate analysis. Mitigation: end-to-end tests in CI and daily reconciliation job.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment infrastructure deployed behind feature flag and canary validated (logs + billing reconciliation).
Analytics events flowing and dashboards created with ownership assigned.
Security playbook drafted, reviewed by Security & Legal, and published to Confluence.
SEs have templated RFQ flows and an automation to attach the security summary to flagged trials.
